$comment: Ground truth for scripts/eval-search.ts. Every entry names the knowledge
documents (and, where one page clearly owns the answer, the pages) that a
good search would surface for that query.
`knowledge` is the primary target: several documents may legitimately answer
the same question, so list every acceptable one — a hit on any of them counts.
`pages` is optional and stricter; it drives the page-level metrics.
`kind` groups queries so the report can show WHERE search is weak rather than
th-question / en-question — a whole sentence, the way an agent phrases it
keyword                   — the two or three words a human types in a hurry
body                      — the answer lives in the page body, not its title
cross-lang                — asked in one language, answered in the other
typo                      — a plausible misspelling of a real term
These ids point at the LIVE database (data/index.db). Editing or deleting the
target documents invalidates the rows that name them; the eval script reports
any target that no longer exists instead of silently scoring it as a miss.
